authority: CEO Round 84 deep audit directive: 'Use: L3-REFUSED — constitutive equivalence gate fails. L3-INVALID — solver fails to converge / output invalid. L3-FAIL — both solvers validly converge on the same problem but disagree beyond tolerance. That state machine is much cleaner.'
purpose: Replace ambiguous L3 status labels (FAIL, INVALID ATTEMPT, NOT VALIDLY TESTED) with a clean four-state machine. Each state has explicit entry conditions and required evidence.

L3-REFUSED.description: The cross-solver comparison is BLOCKED because the constitutive-equivalence gate (CE-GATE-001) failed. No solver execution is permitted until the gate passes.
entry_conditions: CE-GATE-001 returns REFUSE on the audit for this benchmark and solver pair
required_evidence: CE-GATE-001 audit JSON file with at least one of the 8 checks = false
Gate execution log showing REFUSE verdict
permitted_next_actions: Option A: implement exact constitutive replication of solver A's law in solver B (custom term)
Option B: re-freeze a new benchmark version (B003, B004, ...) with a formulation both solvers natively implement
Option C: prove mathematically that the two formulations produce identical SED/stress/tangent over the benchmark deformation range
forbidden_next_actions: Run solver B anyway and compare to solver A (Article VII: never weaken verifier to rescue claim)
Tune solver B until it matches solver A (Article VII)
Silently change material label without updating audit
L3-REFUSED.verdict_meaning: L3 has NOT been tested. The comparison cannot be performed validly at this time.

L3-INVALID.description: The cross-solver comparison was ATTEMPTED but one or both solvers failed to produce a valid converged result. The numerical output cannot be used for comparison.
entry_conditions: AND at least one solver failed to converge OR produced output that violates its own convergence criterion
required_evidence: Solver A output (converged or non-converged, with residual history)
Solver B output (converged or non-converged, with residual history)
Explicit identification of which solver(s) failed
permitted_next_actions: Reconfigure the failing solver (Newton settings, load stepping, etc.) — but NOT constitutive model
Switch to a different benchmark where both solvers can converge
Document as solver-robustness limitation, not physics disagreement
forbidden_next_actions: Declare L3-FAIL based on a comparison involving non-converged output
Tune the failing solver's constitutive model to make it converge
L3-INVALID.verdict_meaning: L3 has been attempted but no valid comparison was produced. The numerical disagreement (if any) is implementation/solver-robustness, NOT physics (Article XXIX).

L3-FAIL.description: Both solvers validly converged on the same frozen benchmark, but their numerical results disagree beyond the pre-registered tolerance. This is a genuine physics disagreement that requires investigation.
entry_conditions: AND solver A converged per its convergence criterion
AND solver B converged per its convergence criterion
AND the relative difference between solver outputs exceeds the pre-registered tolerance
required_evidence: Solver A converged output with residual history
Solver B converged output with residual history
Three-way comparison: Analytical ↔ Solver A ↔ Solver B, with relative differences computed against the analytical reference
Statement of strongest alternative explanation (Article XXXII)
permitted_next_actions: Investigate the cause of disagreement (most likely: subtle constitutive difference not caught by gate, quadrature artifact, or solver path-dependence)
Document the disagreement as a discovery, not a failure
Consider re-freezing the benchmark with stricter equivalence checks
forbidden_next_actions: Tune either solver until they agree (Article VII)
Relax the tolerance to make the disagreement disappear
Declare L3-PASS based on partial agreement
L3-FAIL.verdict_meaning: L3 was validly tested and the solvers genuinely disagree. This is information, not failure. The disagreement itself becomes a discovery.

L3-PASS.description: Both solvers validly converged on the same frozen benchmark AND their numerical results agree within the pre-registered tolerance AND both agree with the independently-derived analytical reference.
entry_conditions: CE-GATE-001 PASSES (constitutive equivalence verified, including tangent)
AND solver A converged per its convergence criterion
AND solver B converged per its convergence criterion
required_evidence: Solver A converged output with residual history
Solver B converged output with residual history
Three-way comparison table with relative differences
Optional: L3-PASS-STRONG if all three differences < tolerance_secondary
permitted_next_actions: Promote Slot 5 from DISCOVERY HYPOTHESIS to L3-VALIDATED
Proceed to Stage -1 virtual fragmentation experiment
Advance to next validation level (L4: FSI, damage, contact, fracture)
forbidden_next_actions: Declare L3-PASS if any required check or evidence is missing
Skip the three-way comparison (analytical is the third leg, not optional)
L3-PASS.verdict_meaning: L3 was validly tested and the solvers agree. The cross-solver validation is complete.

transitions.L3-REFUSED → L3-INVALID: After CE-GATE-001 passes (constitutive equivalence established), attempt solver execution. If either solver fails to converge, transition to L3-INVALID.
transitions.L3-REFUSED → L3-FAIL: After CE-GATE-001 passes, both solvers converge, but results disagree beyond tolerance. Transition to L3-FAIL.
transitions.L3-REFUSED → L3-PASS: After CE-GATE-001 passes, both solvers converge, results agree within tolerance AND with analytical reference. Transition to L3-PASS.
transitions.L3-INVALID → L3-REFUSED: If investigation reveals that the non-convergence was actually due to a constitutive mismatch not caught by the gate, re-run CE-GATE-001 with extended checks. If gate now fails, transition back to L3-REFUSED.
transitions.L3-INVALID → L3-FAIL: If the failing solver is reconfigured (without changing constitutive model) and now converges, but disagrees with the other solver, transition to L3-FAIL.
transitions.L3-INVALID → L3-PASS: If the failing solver is reconfigured and now converges AND agrees, transition to L3-PASS.
transitions.L3-FAIL → L3-REFUSED: If investigation reveals the disagreement was due to a constitutive mismatch, transition back to L3-REFUSED with extended gate checks.
transitions.L3-FAIL → L3-PASS: Generally forbidden. A failed comparison cannot become a pass without re-freezing the benchmark or re-deriving the analytical reference. Re-freeze creates a new benchmark version (B003, B004, ...) and the old L3-FAIL stands as historical record.
transitions.L3-PASS → L3-FAIL: Permitted if a later audit reveals the pass was based on incorrect evidence (e.g., analytical derivation had an error). Requires explicit retraction.

lineage_rule.principle: Each benchmark version is a distinct entity. Results from one version do NOT transfer to another. L3-PASS on B002 does not imply L3-PASS on B003, and vice versa.
lineage_rule.versioning: Benchmark versions are integers: B001 (challenged, archived), B002 (frozen, current), B003 (Sanity 1, frozen this round), B004 (if re-freeze needed for (K/2)(ln J)^2 volumetric).
lineage_rule.promotion_rule: L3-PASS on the LATEST frozen benchmark version is required to promote Slot 5 to L3-VALIDATED. Earlier versions are historical.
